title: One Sentence Each · Teams
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play One Sentence Each · Teams with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose two players and a simple starting situation. The lead and partner alternate one sentence each until they have said four sentences. The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending. Form two teams. Each team has four turns; only the lead’s teammates respond or assist. Each success earns the team one point. The higher team score wins; ties are shared.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4–8 players; materials: None.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In One Sentence Each, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
recall.why: The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending.
